name: MeLBench

name: CreativeMashup
rejection_reason: Data access barrier - benchmark not ready for automated evaluation. CogSci 2025, arXiv:2504.13120; 'Probing and Inducing Combinational Creativity in Vision-Language Models'; CreativeMashup benchmark tests VLMs' understanding of combinational creativity through 666 artist-generated visual mashups; uses Identification-Explanation-Implication (IEI) framework with three task levels: (1) Identification - identify two primary objects combined in mashup, (2) Explanation - identify attributes enabling combination, (3) Implication - interpret semantic meaning/message; evaluation uses open-ended responses evaluated by GPT-4o as judge (85.1% and 81.6% consistency with human experts); **Key blockers**: (a) Full dataset (666 examples) only available via Google Drive manual download at https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XIvOVwP0eVX60L-STugt_vi19Q_kAEMW, not programmatically accessible; (b) GitHub repo (PPYYQQ/aicc-code) contains only 40 examples used for generation task human study, not the comprehension task; (c) No JSON annotations file with prompts/ground truth for the 666-example comprehension benchmark; (d) Paper does not specify exact prompt templates for the three IEI task levels, only conceptual descriptions; (e) Evaluation requires LLM-as-judge implementation (GPT-4o adjudicator) not yet configured; (f) Images are visual mashups combining objects (e.g., pepper + fire extinguisher), requiring multimodal evaluation; **Precedent**: Similar to MARS benchmark (line 874 in LEARNINGS.md) rejected for 'images not yet released'; **Future potential**: Once authors release full dataset with annotations on HuggingFace or provide programmatic Google Drive access (like ARN using gdown), and specify exact prompts, this would be a strong candidate for multimodal onboarding using MediaObject pattern (like MEMECAP); Multimodal (vision-language); requires HEIM/VHELM framework; GitHub: PPYYQQ/aicc-code; Project page: ppyyqq.github.io/aicc

name: Diversity vs. Recognizability Framework
